content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to recent price spikes; fails to anticipate or amplify momentum after sharp increases.
- Overestimation is more pronounced in high-volatility periods (e.g., post-2024-10-16).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects downward after spikes, underestimating continuation of upward trends.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle to late horizon.
- Model fails to capture long-term trend persistence; underestimates sustained upward momentum in multi-day rallies.
- Overestimation is more severe in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting model overconfident in short-term decline assumptions.
